title: When Ice Crystals Spark: The Hidden Science of Thunderstorms
title_zh: 当冰晶迸出火花：雷暴背后的隐藏科学
intro_zh: 本文约527词，属于CET-4难度，介绍雷暴云中的电荷形成、闪电与雷声的原理、雷暴的作用及安全常识。

paragraphs.en: Thunderstorms are common in summer, yet they are among nature's most complex weather systems. Inside a tall storm cloud, tiny ice crystals and softer ice pellets are thrown around by strong rising air. As they bump into one another, electrons are pulled from one particle and added to another. This simple contact slowly builds up electric charge. The process helps separate positive and negative charges within the cloud.
paragraphs.zh: 雷暴在夏季很常见，却是自然界最复杂的天气系统之一。在高大的雷暴云内部，强烈的上升气流把微小的冰晶和较软的冰粒抛来抛去。它们相互碰撞时，电子会从一个粒子转移到另一个粒子上。这种简单的接触逐渐积累起电荷。这一过程有助于在云内把正电荷和负电荷分开。

paragraphs.en: Usually, the top of the cloud becomes positively charged, while the lower part holds negative charge. The ground below is then pulled into a positive state. Like a stretched rubber band, the air between these opposite charges stores energy. Most of the time, the air acts as a good insulator and keeps the charges apart. But the tension keeps growing.
paragraphs.zh: 通常，云的顶部带正电，而下部带负电。下方的地面因此被感应出正电状态。就像拉紧的橡皮筋，这些相反电荷之间的空气储存着能量。大多数时候，空气是良好的绝缘体，使电荷彼此隔开。但这种张力不断增大。

paragraphs.en: When the electric field becomes strong enough, the air can no longer hold it back. A faint, invisible path called a stepped leader reaches down in quick jumps. When it nears the ground, a bright return stroke rushes upward. This is the flash we see. A lightning channel can heat the air to about 30,000°C—five times hotter than the sun's surface. The sudden discharge carries currents of roughly 30,000 amperes. The whole event may last less than a second.
paragraphs.zh: 当电场强到一定程度，空气再也无法阻止它。一条微弱而看不见的通道——阶梯先导——以快速跳跃的方式向下延伸。当它接近地面时，一道明亮的回击向上冲去。这就是我们看到的闪电。闪电通道能把空气加热到约3万摄氏度——比太阳表面还热五倍。突然的放电携带约3万安培的电流。整个过程可能持续不到一秒。

paragraphs.en: That extreme heat creates a different effect: thunder. The air expands in a fraction of a second, producing a shock wave that we hear as a rumble or a sharp crack. Because light travels far faster than sound, we always see lightning before we hear it. A simple rule helps estimate distance: every three seconds between flash and sound means the storm is about one kilometre away.
paragraphs.zh: 这种极端高温产生了另一种效应：雷声。空气在几分之一秒内膨胀，产生冲击波，我们听到的就是隆隆声或尖锐的爆裂声。因为光传播得比声音快得多，所以我们总是先看到闪电后听到雷声。一个简单的规则有助于估算距离：闪电和雷声之间每相隔三秒，意味着雷暴大约在一公里之外。

paragraphs.en: Not all lightning is the same. Most flashes stay inside the cloud, jumping between charged regions. Cloud-to-ground strikes are less common but more dangerous. A positive strike, which comes from the upper part of the storm, can be especially powerful and may reach farther than expected. Around the world, about 44 lightning flashes happen every second—nearly four million a day.
paragraphs.zh: 并非所有闪电都一样。大多数闪电留在云内，在带电区域之间跳跃。云地闪较少见，但更危险。正地闪来自雷暴的上部，可能特别强大，而且可能比预期延伸得更远。全世界每秒大约发生44次闪电——每天近400万次。

paragraphs.en: Thunderstorms also do useful work. Lightning helps turn nitrogen in the air into forms that plants can use, acting like a natural fertilizer. It can clean the air and produce ozone high in the atmosphere. In this way, a storm may leave the soil richer than it found it. Yet the same energy demands respect. A single strike can damage a tree or a building and start a fire.
paragraphs.zh: 雷暴也会做有益的工作。闪电帮助把空气中的氮转化为植物可以利用的形式，就像天然肥料。它能净化空气，并在大气高处产生臭氧。这样一来，一场风暴可能让土壤比之前更肥沃。然而，同样的能量也要求我们保持敬畏。一次雷击就能损坏树木或建筑物，甚至引发火灾。

paragraphs.en: Safety begins with paying attention. If you can hear thunder, you are already close enough to be at risk. Move into a solid building or a hard-topped car, and keep away from open fields, tall trees and water. A shelter is not just a place to stay dry; it is protection from a possible strike. Waiting 30 minutes after the last thunder is a wise habit.
paragraphs.zh: 安全始于留意。如果你能听到雷声，你就已经离得足够近，面临风险。进入坚固的建筑或硬顶汽车，远离开阔田野、高树和水面。避难所不只是躲雨的地方；它能保护你免受可能的雷击。最后一声雷后再等30分钟，是明智的习惯。

paragraphs.en: Scientists now track storms with radar, satellites and lightning sensors. These tools show where charges are building and help warn people earlier. Better warnings can save lives and reduce damage to power lines and homes. The more we understand the electric cloud above us, the better we can enjoy its amazing show—and stay out of harm's way.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家现在用雷达、卫星和闪电传感器追踪风暴。这些工具显示电荷在哪里积累，并帮助更早地向人们发出预警。更好的预警能拯救生命，减少对电线和房屋的损害。我们越了解头顶的带电云层，就越能欣赏它令人惊叹的表演——同时远离危险。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: It explains how thunderstorms form lightning and how people can stay safe.
It compares summer storms with winter storms in detail.
It argues that lightning is more useful than harmful.
It describes the history of weather forecasting.
questions.explain: 文章整体介绍雷暴云中的电荷形成、闪电与雷声的原理、雷暴的作用及安全常识，选项A最全面。

questions.q: According to paragraph 1, what happens when ice crystals and ice pellets collide?
options: They turn into rain at once.
Electrons move between them and build up charge.
They stop the rising air inside the cloud.
They make the cloud top negatively charged.
questions.explain: 第一段明确指出，冰晶和冰粒碰撞时电子从一个粒子转移到另一个粒子，逐渐积累电荷。

questions.q: Why does the author mention the three-second rule?
options: To show how to count lightning flashes.
To explain why thunder is louder than lightning.
To help readers estimate how far a storm is.
To prove that sound travels faster than light.
questions.explain: 第四段提到，闪电和雷声之间每相隔三秒，说明雷暴约在一公里外，因此该规则用于估算距离。

questions.q: The word shelter in paragraph 7 is closest in meaning to ____.
questions.explain: 第七段说shelter不只是躲雨的地方，还能保护人免受雷击，因此其含义是提供保护的地方。
